    Inverting an endomorphism on a module of finite length #

    source
    theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.bijective_precomp_iff_of_isCompl {R : Type u_1} {M : Type u} {N : Type v} [Ring R] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] (a : Module.End R M) (h : IsCompl (LinearMap.ker a) (LinearMap.range a)) :
    (Function.Bijective fun (f : M →ₗ[R] N) => f ∘ₗ a) ↔ Subsingleton (↥(LinearMap.ker a) →ₗ[R] N)

    When kernel and image are complementary, inverting an endomorphism by precomposition amounts to killing all maps out of its kernel.

    source
    theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.exists_fitting_inversion {R : Type u_1} {M : Type u} [Ring R] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [IsArtinian R M] [IsNoetherian R M] (a : Module.End R M) :
    ∃ n > 0, IsCompl (a ^ n).ker (a ^ n).range ∧ ∀ (N : Type u_2) [inst : AddCommGroup N] [inst_1 : Module R N], (Function.Bijective fun (f : M →ₗ[R] N) => f ∘ₗ a) ↔ Subsingleton (↥(a ^ n).ker →ₗ[R] N)

    A single Fitting summand works simultaneously for all target modules.

      Inverting a noninvertible endomorphism of a projective module of finite length on arbitrary targets cuts out the modules over one proper quotient.

      Ring maps whose restricted modules invert the endomorphism factor uniquely through the Fitting trace quotient. One simple module of the original ring is excluded.
